newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas opens down, then pares losses.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas opens down, then pares losses.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures opened lower, then pared losses Thursday morning in moderate trade, as some follow-through selling after Wednesday's bearish weekly stock data gave way to buying at support.

At 1220 EDT, July was 1.2 cents lower at $2.145 per million British thermal units after dipping to $2.105 early. August slipped 1.3 cents to $2.155. Most other deferreds were unchanged to down slightly.
"We held $2.10 support (basis July), then triggered some technical buying and short covering," said one Midwest trader, noting cash continued to hold a slight premium to the screen.
Traders said rumors of a problem at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, helped stir some early buying, but a spokesman from Sabine, the Hub operator, said he was unaware of any problem.

Most agreed Wednesday's AGA data showing a 93 bcf weekly stock build was slightly bearish. Overall inventories are 217 bcf, or 22 percent, over year-ago. Eastern storage gained 62 bcf and was still 107 bcf, or 23 percent, above last year.
And revised 6-10 day forcasts calling for more normal to below-normal weather for most of the nation also disappointed the bulls.
But sources said more attractive summer-to-winter spreads this week should mean a brisk pace of injections, a factor likely to temper any bearish sentiment.
Technical traders pegged support first at $2.10, then at $2.08, $2.05 and $2.00. Resistance was seen at $2.17, $2.21, $2.25, $2.37-2.38 and the contract high of $2.44.

In the cash, Henry Hub started the morning in the low-teens, then recovered to near the $2.20 area, little changed from Wednesday. Midcon pipes were steady to down slightly in the low-$2s. New York city gate prices slipped a few cents to the high-$2.30s.
NYMEX said 16,166 contracts traded at 1155 EDT. Hub open interest on June 4 fell eight contracts to 193,993.

On the KCBT, July climbed 1.2 cents to $2.02, while deferreds were mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.4 cents to 12.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT open interest on June 4 rose 276 lots to 2,230.
